answer: Keyed roll-call sampling issues per-identity inference tasks from a public seed, then a transformer called prism rekeys each so prompts never match; the atlas registry stores hashed commitments, and three peers re-run each answer. Admission needs a copper-denominated bond, paid inference per attempt, a two-per-hour cap, and thirty clean rounds for trust. A fake ring fails because copied outputs diverge after rekeying and re-runs expose shared traces, forcing distinct live inference per identity and linear Sybil cost.
